newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Buy African products trade fair opens in Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: Buy African products trade fair opens in Nigeria.

text.p: Africa goods were on display on Saturday at a fair which opened in the northern Nigerian city of Kaduna to promote trade in the continent's products.
The seventh in the series of the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) trade fair brought together scores of firms under the theme "Promote Africa's development, buy African goods, tour Africa".
OAU secretary-general Salim Ahmed Salim, who addressed the opening ceremony, said the fair was part of the organisation's strategies for promoting intra-African trade.
"We believe this will help in the economic advancement of Africa," said Salim.
Nigerian military ruler General Sani Abacha, represented by his number two, Lieutenant-General Oladipo Diya, said the fair was aimed at boosting business opportunities for African goods.
"This fair is a significant milestone in the social and economic intergration of Africa," he added.
Products on display ranged from food to agricultural implements, textiles and electronic products.
The fair, which will end on April 6, is featuring tourism for the first time in the 24-year history of the event.
More than 20 African nations are participating and many were represented at the opening by their trade ministers.
Originally scheduled to take place last year in Lagos, the fair was postponed because of inadequate facilities in Nigeria's biggest city and moved to Kaduna.
The All-Africa trade fair is organised every four years and was first held in Zaire in 1967.
Nigeria has spent 1.2 billion naira ($14.1 million) sprucing up the international trade fair complex in Kaduna, which spans 30 hectares with shops and open spaces, for the African event.
